problems.quote: Every call to a language model is billed on tokens
problems.issue: Not for flat-rate plans, reserved capacity or self-hosting. Even on metered APIs, the example’s 76,500 tokens/month is a volume estimate, not a bill: it assumes one load per session and omits price classes.
problems.fix: Count actual requests, not sessions. Reconcile fresh input, cache reads/writes, billable reasoning, output and fees against invoices; distinguish cash savings from freed capacity.

problems.quote: Below roughly 50 to 100 sources, retrieval wins
problems.issue: Source count alone predicts neither cost nor answer quality. Five stable manuals queried hourly can justify synthesis; thousands of rarely queried files may not.
problems.fix: Measure ingest and refresh cost against query frequency times the measured per-query saving, at matched accuracy.

problems.quote: The quote check (R6), which ties every claim to a source line.
problems.issue: A substring check covers recognised quotes, not unquoted claims, omitted qualifications or entailment. The planted failure also says nothing about model-reviewer miss rates.
problems.fix: Describe R6 as quote-presence checking. Test missing citations separately and sample claim–passage pairs for support.

problems.quote: python tools/kb.py lint` - repeat until it exits 0.
problems.issue: As documented, R7 flags a changed raw hash until `done` updates it, but `done` comes after lint. A correct page edit cannot clear that finding; an agent may pay to retry indefinitely.
problems.fix: Lint against a staged manifest and generated index, recheck the source hash, then publish together. Cap repair attempts and surface unresolved errors.

problems.issue: A status failure with empty stdout becomes a successful zero-line count; a broken nightly ingest looks like a quiet night.
problems.fix: Use `pending=$(python3 tools/kb.py status) || exit 1`, retain stderr, and skip inference only on successful empty output. Call that zero model spend, not zero job cost.

problems.quote: Allow-list the exact commands (`python3 tools/kb.py *`, `git add *`, `git commit *`)
problems.issue: Those are wildcard patterns, not exact commands. Broad staging or `git add -A` can commit unrelated changes or secrets.
problems.fix: Use an isolated worktree and a trusted wrapper with fixed operations and validated paths. Inspect the staged diff before committing.

problems.quote: climb one rung at a time
problems.issue: The rungs mix model capability, tool access and parallelism; they are not ordered by total cost or correctness. Repeated failed attempts can cost more than direct routing.
problems.fix: Compare cost per accepted result including fallback, latency and human review. Skip known-inadequate routes and periodically retest the learned floor.

problems.quote: does every statement follow from its source?
problems.issue: The verifier diagram supplies summaries and claims, not original passages. Fresh context cannot recover a qualification omitted by a worker or guarantee independent judgement.
problems.fix: Give the verifier read access to cited spans plus surrounding context; check coverage against the task, not just support for retained claims. Include verification in fan-out pricing.

problems.issue: The cache can publish a partial file to concurrent readers. The example also lacks expiry and access scoping: identical text need not have the same authorised or current answer.
problems.fix: Cache only validated, reusable results; scope keys by access domain and dependency versions, enforce retention, and publish atomically.

problems.quote: Independent reviews of small month-long trials report mixed results
problems.issue: No reviews or measurements are cited. Likewise, the supplied material indexes chapters 11–13 but omits their bodies and the tool/test sources; it cannot substantiate all receipts or establish novelty against those missing chapters.
problems.fix: Link dated trials and their workloads. Supply the missing chapters and a pinned, runnable revision; treat the extensions below as new relative to the visible material.

keep: Measure, then spend effort where the money is.
No shared writes. Workers return text; one process writes files.
Never trim safety or compliance instructions to save tokens.
It checks structure and quotes, not truth.

techniques.name: Debounce superseded requests
techniques.saves: For draft previews or live tagging, avoid launching inference on intermediate edits that nobody will consume.
techniques.risk: Adds preview latency; dropping revisions is wrong for audit events, explicit submissions or tasks where every revision matters.

tool.algorithm:
Read JSONL draft events with tenant, document, monotone revision, timestamp and submit flag.
Keep the newest pending revision per key; use a heap of quiet-period deadlines, ignoring obsolete timers.
Emit one job at expiry or immediately on submit; tag results with revision so late previews cannot replace newer ones.

techniques.name: Coalesce concurrent misses
techniques.saves: A completed-result cache still pays for simultaneous cold requests. Single-flight dispatch pays for one generation and delivers it to all waiters.
techniques.risk: Sharing is wrong for independent samples, side effects or different permissions; a stalled leader delays its waiters.

tool.algorithm:
Read eligible requests; hash authorised scope, complete versioned request and generation settings. Bypass independent-sample requests.
Under a threading.Lock, map the key to one concurrent.futures.Future; only its creator submits inference outside the lock.
Deliver the same result or error to waiting request IDs, bound waiter time, and remove the entry on completion.

techniques.name: Repair failed fields, not whole records
techniques.saves: On a partially valid extraction, regenerate only rejected independent fields instead of paying for a full response again.
techniques.risk: A valid-looking field can still be wrong; patching dependent fields separately can leave contradictory records.

tool.algorithm:
Read original evidence, output JSON, field validators and declared dependency groups; identify failing groups.
Emit one patch request with allowed field paths, constraints and evidence for those groups; keep accepted values locally.
Merge only allow-listed paths, rerun field and whole-record checks, and send unresolved records to review.

techniques.name: Generate changes instead of copying a document
techniques.saves: For localised revisions, emit only replacement spans; Python reconstructs the full deliverable without billing unchanged text as output.
techniques.risk: Poor fit for global rewrites. A stale base or ambiguous edit location can silently change the wrong passage.

tool.algorithm:
Read a versioned document; emit its digest and numbered paragraphs as an edit contract for the model.
Accept JSON edits keyed by original paragraph ranges; reject stale digest, overlaps, missing targets and out-of-bounds ranges.
Apply replacements in reverse order; emit reconstructed document and unified diff for acceptance checks.

techniques.name: Train a local classifier with abstention
techniques.saves: For a stable, high-volume label taxonomy, a small supervised classifier can eliminate even cheap model calls on familiar cases.
techniques.risk: Rare labels, changing vocabulary and biased training labels hurt accuracy; a high score alone is not evidence of correctness.

tool.algorithm:
Read labelled JSONL split by time into train, calibration and test sets; fit smoothed multinomial naive Bayes with re, collections.Counter and math.log.
On calibration data choose per-label score-margin thresholds meeting a precision target with minimum support; disable unsupported labels and independently test.
For each new text emit a local label or abstain to the existing model on low margin or low vocabulary coverage; log decisions for sampled review.

workflows.name: Latest-revision draft previews
steps: Replay timestamped edit bursts to choose a quiet period within the preview latency target.
Debounce per authorised document; bypass the timer on explicit submit.
Coalesce identical eligible in-flight jobs and display only the current revision.
Compare billed calls per completed document, stale displays and p95 preview latency against immediate dispatch.

workflows.name: Patch-only document maintenance
steps: Snapshot the source and define which sections may change.
Request anchored replacements rather than a rewritten document.
Reject stale or overlapping patches; reconstruct locally and review the diff against the requested change.
Compare output spend per accepted revision, including rejected patches and full-rewrite fallbacks.

workflows.name: Selective ticket triage and extraction
steps: Train and test the local labeler on historical tickets; keep sensitive categories on mandatory review.
Serve supported labels locally, send abstentions for model classification, then request only the extraction required for the chosen category.
Patch invalid independent fields once; route remaining failures to review.
Blind-audit local accepts as well as fallbacks. Disable a label if precision drops; track total spend per correctly completed ticket.
